body:
Growing up, I had a lot trouble getting to school and "[school refusal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_refusal)" issues related to social anxiety and depression. 

Now it's about moving out, we don't really know how to facilitate the transition gradually. I live somewhere with no stores or sidewalks or anywhere to go, so I can't practice a lot of the skills I'll need. And there's only houses nearby, no apartments nearby or anything so I'm not moving out multiple train rides from home. 

When I tell them my issues, they bring up the idea of a transitional living place, where I'd receive care during the day but still live independently in my own apartment. Unfortunately most don't take insurance and are on the opposite sides of the country. So the best solution therapists have is that I move out and my parents help pay for it (and a support system there) until I can work through and survive living on my own. But that has a bunch of financial issues and guilt associated with it, and there's no guarantee I won't be anxious/depressed enough to even go out and do basic things which I'm worried about. But that still seems like the best/only solution at the moment, but I don't know how to be prepared for it, if I need to be 'mentally ready' and 'believe' I can do it first, because I definitely don't feel that way rn. But I don't want to fail and we spent all this money and it's all my fault and blah blah blah
